about: Every change between SDK 2 and SDK 3, as data. kind: "renamed" = the same call under a new name (mechanical: true means a script may rename it: same arguments, same result unless a "list" entry for the new name says otherwise); "removed" = no like-for-like call, the note says what to do ("to" names the nearest replacement); "option" = an option or argument that went; "option" entries with "argument" name the position (0 = first) of an argument a script may drop when it is the last one passed; "list" = a function that now returns ListResult<T> = { items, nextCursor, count? } ("paged" says whether it takes limit + cursor); "behaviour" = something that changes at run time and the compiler cannot see.

hold.when: The app calls a writing function of the old `attestation` namespace (singular): attestation.create, attestation.update, attestation.remove.
hold.why: Its data has not been moved to the new `attestations` yet. SDK 3 keeps the namespace so the app still builds; leave those calls as they are.

unchanged: The old `attestation` namespace (deprecated, kept until its data is moved).
`ctx.sl.*` inside an app's server functions: it runs on the server and keeps its shapes.
The standard query functions (proof.query, contact.query, products.standardQuery, app.records.query).
Every function that is not a list and was not deprecated.

changes.name: product.get
changes.note: The whole `product` namespace (singular) is gone: use `products`.

changes.name: product.list
changes.note: Then treat it as a list: `products.list` returns ListResult<ProductResponse>.

changes.name: product.listAssets
changes.note: Then treat it as a list: `products.listAssets` returns ListResult<AssetResponse>.

changes.name: ai.generateContent
changes.note: A different call: it takes chat messages, not `contents`, and answers in the chat-completions shape (`choices[0].message.content`). `ai.chat.completions.create(collectionId, { messages: [{ role: "user", content }] })`.

changes.name: Asset.thumbnails
changes.note: One thumbnail address (`string | null`), not a map of sizes.

changes.name: asset.uploadAsset
changes.note: Takes one options object: `asset.upload({ file, scope, … })` (type UploadAssetOptions).

changes.name: BatchCreateRequest.id
changes.note: The server generates the batch id. Don't send one.

changes.name: comms.queryRecipientsWithAction
changes.note: It posted to an address the API never had, so it never worked. The real call takes `interactionId` (not `actionId`) and returns a list of ids, or of `{ id, outcome }` with `includeOutcome: true`.

changes.name: comms.queryRecipientsWithoutAction
changes.note: It posted to an address the API never had, so it never worked. The real call takes `interactionId` (not `actionId`) and returns a list of ids.

changes.name: CommsRecipientsWithActionQuery
changes.note: `actionId` is `interactionId`.

changes.name: CommsRecipientsWithoutActionQuery
changes.note: `actionId` is `interactionId`.

changes.name: evaluateCondition
changes.note: Takes the field's whole condition list: `evaluateConditions(property.conditions, property.showWhen, values)`.

changes.name: FirebaseTimestamp
changes.note: Dates are ISO 8601 strings or a Date: `BatchCreateRequest.expiryDate` and `BatchUpdateRequest.expiryDate` are `string | Date`.

changes.name: order.findByProduct
changes.note: The API never had this address, so the call could only fail. Use `order.query(collectionId, { query: { productId } })`.

changes.name: order.findItemsByProduct
changes.note: The API never had this address, so the call could only fail. Use `order.query(collectionId, { query: { productId }, includeItems: true })` and read each order's items.

changes.name: order.findOrdersByProduct
changes.note: The API never had this address, so the call could only fail. Use `order.query(collectionId, { query: { productId } })`.

changes.name: order.getOrderIdsByAttribute
changes.note: The API never had this address, so the call could only fail. Use `order.query` with `productId`, `batchId` or `variantId` in `query`, and read the ids from `items`.

changes.name: order.lookup
changes.note: The API never had this address, so the call could only fail. Find the orders that hold items with `order.query(collectionId, { query: { items: [{ itemType, itemId }] } })`.

changes.name: product.find
changes.note: A different body (type ProductQueryRequest). Returns a list and pages with `limit` + `cursor`.

changes.name: product.publicFind
changes.note: Use `products.get` when you know the id, `products.query` to search. The server retired this route some time ago.

changes.name: realtime.getAdminToken
changes.note: The SDK gets its own tokens. Subscribe with `realtime.onMine(scope, onMessage)`.

changes.name: realtime.getPublicToken
changes.note: The SDK gets its own tokens. Subscribe with `realtime.channel(scope, name)` or `realtime.onChange(scope, filter, onChange)`.

changes.name: site.ready
changes.note: Sites are server-rendered and nothing waits for the signal. Delete the call.

changes.name: VariantCreateRequest.id
changes.note: The server generates the variant id. Don't send one.

changes.name: asset.list
changes.note: No asset list ever read it, so it never filtered anything. Filter the items you get back (`a.mimeType?.startsWith('image/')`), or as an admin use `asset.listAdmin` with `assetType`.

changes.name: authKit.list
changes.note: There is no public list of AuthKit configs, so the call without `true` always failed. Call `authKit.list(collectionId)`.

changes.name: bookings.mine
changes.note: `mine` is always the caller's own bookings. To list a contact's bookings as an admin use `bookings.list`.

changes.name: collection.list
changes.note: There is no public list of collections, so `collection.list(false)` always failed. Call `collection.list()`: it lists the collections the signed-in user can work on.

changes.name: comms.queryRecipientIds
changes.note: The server never read it. For one journey step's recipients use `journeysAnalytics.recipients`.

changes.name: containers.publicList
changes.note: The public list is always the active containers.

changes.name: containers.publicList
changes.note: The public list never filtered by ref.

changes.name: facets.list
changes.note: The list never read it: a facet list has no values. Read one facet with `facets.get(…, { includeValues: true })`, or its values with `facets.listValues`.

changes.name: facets.publicList
changes.note: The list never read it. Read a facet's values with `facets.publicListValues`.

changes.name: interactions.publicMyInteractions
changes.note: The server never read it.

changes.name: lots.publicList
changes.note: Admin only: use `lots.list`.

changes.name: adminCards.list
changes.note: `cards` is `items`; `hidden` and `layout` stay beside it.

changes.name: ai.agent.listTools
changes.note: `tools` is `items`.

changes.name: ai.skills.list
changes.note: `skills` is `items`.

changes.name: attestation.list

changes.name: authKit.listTrustedDevices

changes.note: The tags are in `items`; the claim set's own fields (id, name, …) stay beside them.

changes.name: claimSet.ranges.tags

changes.name: containers.listItems
changes.note: Pages only with `history: true`; the current contents come back whole.

changes.after: ListResult<{ facet, values }> & { buckets: FacetBucket[], meta? }

changes.note: `results` is `items`; `query` and `mode` stay beside it.

changes.name: knowledge.search
changes.note: `results` is `items`; `query` and `mode` stay beside it.

changes.name: location.search
changes.note: The old `count` was the number of rows returned; it is gone.

changes.name: lots.listProducts
changes.note: `total` is `count`.

changes.name: order.getLocationHistory
changes.note: The old `count` was the number of rows returned; it is gone.

changes.name: order.getTimeline
changes.note: The old `count` was the number of rows returned; it is gone.

changes.name: order.list
changes.note: Now sends `direction` and `partyId`, which SDK 2 accepted and silently dropped.

changes.name: order.query
changes.note: `limit` and `cursor` go at the top level of the body.

changes.name: products.query
changes.before: { items, page: { limit, offset, returned, total, hasMore, nextCursor }, meta }
changes.note: The nested `page` option is gone: `limit` and `cursor` go at the top level of the body. `page.total` is `count`.

changes.name: proof.findByProduct
changes.note: Not paged: it returns the newest `limit` (default 100), or every proof matching `filterBy`. Page through proofs with `proof.query`.

changes.note: `secrets` is `items`.

changes.name: secrets.listOwn
changes.note: `secrets` is `items`.

changes.name: segments.recipients
changes.note: `total` is `count`.

changes.name: serviceAccounts.list

changes.note: `total` is `count`.

changes.name: shop.admin.listPrices
changes.note: `total` is `count`.

changes.name: subscriptions.admin.list

changes.note: `total` is `count`.

changes.note: `passes` is `items`; `ok` is gone.

changes.name: wallet.mine
changes.note: `passes` is `items`; `ok` is gone.

changes.name: error codes
changes.note: Every error code is UPPER_SNAKE (`segments.list.failed` is now `SEGMENTS_LIST_FAILED`). Find string comparisons against `errorCode`, `details.errorCode` and `details.error`. Check `error.errorCode`; never match on message text.

changes.name: error statuses
changes.note: "Not signed in" sent as 400 by some routes is now 401. "Signed in but not allowed" sent as 401 by some routes is now 403. `isAuthError()` covers both.

changes.name: initializeApi({ apiVersion })
changes.note: A version older than 2027-01 is ignored: SDK 3 always asks for at least its own version.

changes.name: paging by offset
changes.note: There is no offset or page number. Page forward with `cursor`; cache keys built on offset or page must use the cursor. For a numbered pager use the standard query.

changes.name: shared dependencies
changes.note: Built on SDK 3, a component declares shared-dependency contract v8 and gets SDK 3 from the host. The window global is `SL3` (and `SmartlinksAuthUI3`); `SL` stays SDK 2.

changes.name: unknown list options
changes.note: A list refuses a query option it does not read (400 UNKNOWN_PARAMETER) instead of ignoring it. Watch for one options object shared by an admin call and a public call (includeDeleted, contactId, assignedTo; status, includeScheduled and includeExpired on public app records).
